speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the rash on your upper extremities: what does it look like, how does it feel, and when did it first appear? Also, have you noticed any fever or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pityriasis Rosea.

Based on your description of a persistent, pruritic rash on the upper extremities for five months without systemic symptoms, this presentation is highly consistent with Pityriasis Rosea. The chronic nature and lack of resolution despite the absence of new triggers support this clinical impression.

REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of the rash to look for the "herald patch" or characteristic "Christmas tree" distribution.
